entries:
### Additions and New Features

- Split the common Compose topology from the ordinary local-development overlay. The default
  lifecycle and local disposable owners now use base plus local development (then SMTP when
  selected), while the live-demo browser owner remains base plus its TLS overlay without a local
  identity bind. Live bootstrap still creates its seed, invitation, Question ID, and claim inputs
  but no longer creates local-file credentials or an authentication host-file setting.
- Accepted WP-PROF-T2 with 2026081807_teaching_operations.sql immutable. Course groups,
  purpose-specific allow/warn policies, referenced-group refusal, atomic S5/S3 re-evaluation with
  sealed receipt history, operator-owned Instructor approval, target-bound 30-day co-instructor
  invitations, direct-membership acceptance, final-Instructor protection, server-owned retention,
  and server-derived preview boundaries are complete. Final Validation passed check_rust,
  check_codebase (5 checks, 301 Node tests), pytest (5,481), built Playwright (245/245, zero
  skips), the fresh 43-migration PostgreSQL baseline with all T2 live oracles, local_stack
  acceptance, T2 visual capture (2/2), UI corpus verification (42/42), both diff checks, and
  independent final reviews with no unresolved P0--P3 finding.
- Repaired the local-stack lifecycle so an ordinary start replaces the project-owned containers
  instead of accumulating them. Startup now removes orphans, recreates dependencies before
  force-recreating application services, and waits for semantic readiness. Scoped image cleanup
  removes inactive project aliases and prunes unused images, while named data volumes remain under
  the existing explicit reset contract. Permanent lifecycle/image-cleanup tests pass, and two
  consecutive starts replaced all nine containers without increasing container, image, or volume
  counts.
- Continued WP-PROF-T2 through the typed domain, Store, Memory, PostgreSQL, and migration
  boundaries. Course groups now retain five purpose-specific multiple-membership policies, reject
  referenced deletion, and atomically re-resolve active S5/S3 work after audience, membership,
  purpose, or M2--M4 changes while preserving sealed receipt generations. Global Instructor
  approval remains non-authorizing operator eligibility; target-bound 30-day co-instructor
  invitations create ordinary direct Instructor membership only after approval recheck and refuse
  removal of the final active Instructor.
- Added the in-progress 2026081807_teaching_operations.sql migration and its disposable PostgreSQL
  upgrade, group-policy, and teaching-authority oracles. The final database-baseline rerun passed all
  43 tracked migrations, exact group receipt transitions, four approval/invitation/concurrency
  cases, forced-RLS and global-table inventory checks, and representative role denial. This is an
  intermediate database vertical receipt; WP-PROF-T2 server, browser, retention-page, full
  Validation, and final independent-review gates remain open.
- Added accepted typed U-, M-, and CI- public locators for accounts, course-membership
  episodes, and co-instructor invitations. Authorized Memory and PostgreSQL projections now keep
  account lookup session-bound, membership lookup exact-course Instructor-bound, and pending
  invitations target-bound; bounded snapshot lists return display labels without email or UUIDs.
  PostgreSQL identity sequences remain least-privilege (ple_auth for accounts and ple_app for
  memberships and invitations), and fresh independent review found no remaining P0--P3 issue.
- Accepted the strict WP-PROF-T2 teaching-operations wire contract before route implementation.
  Group, modifier, preview, co-instructor, and retention DTOs use only typed human references and
  bounded values; strong revisions remain in If-Match, denied previews cannot carry resolved S3
  fields, and retention shapes match the existing server-owned lifecycle endpoints. Temporary
  TypeScript generation emitted 272 concrete types with no unresolved generic or private identity.

### Decisions and Failures

- Accepted WP-PROF-LD1 on 2026-08-20: base_course_installation now owns the typed two-phase Base
  Course lifecycle, while learning-data-access owns its SQL, advisory lock, durable state, migration,
  and Store boundary and project-tools remains the direct CLI adapter. The final PostgreSQL 17 plus
  MinIO lifecycle proved five ordinary accounts across two courses, interruption/resume, retained
  restarts, concurrent serialization, fail-closed mixed state, and fresh regeneration. WP-PROF-LD2
  made WP-PROF-LD2 the next professor handoff; T3 remains parked. LD2's 2026081809 and
  2026081810 allocations were later found to need 1809 scope reconciliation: the current 1809
  file contains approval-candidate discovery and a completed-installation-generation read broker.
  The selector and passkey ceremony seams remain non-schema; the generation-read broker awaits an
  authority ruling. Whole live-demo Validation remains incomplete until LD2 and the connected goal
  close.

- Recorded the intermediate WP-PROF-T2 contract/allocation gate before implementation. The shared
  migration ledger reserves 2026081807 for future
  2026081807_teaching_operations.sql; the professor plan and durable guidance now define
  many-to-many group warning policy, referenced-group refusal, atomic S5/S3 re-evaluation,
  operator-owned non-authorizing Instructor approval, target-bound 30-day co-instructor invitations,
  direct-membership acceptance, final-Instructor protection, and server-owned preview/retention
  boundaries. This documentation gate makes no code, schema, test, or acceptance claim.

entries:
### Behavior or Interface Changes

- Added data-driven platform installation guidance for primary Claude and Codex targets plus
  maintained Cursor and OpenCode compatibility targets. INSTALL.md now documents
  declared destinations, platform references, the guided installer, and repository-first
  replacement.
- Renamed abbreviated public skill-category directories to descriptive names. Category discovery,
  validation, index generation, and permanent tests use direct CATEGORY.md metadata rather than
  a category roster; hidden runtime trees stay outside tracked-source discovery. Removed the
  mistakenly tracked system-skill copy from the public inventory.

### Fixes and Maintenance

- Made the main install_skills.py CLI a guided repository-root interview rather than a
  mode-based command. Shared runtime modules now live in the root install_lib/
  package with no installer import dependency on ; the interview shows destinations and
  applies only after final approval.
- Removed the alternate-home interview question because normal installations always target the
  current operating-system home. No replacement command-line flag was added; the E2E supplies a
  standard temporary HOME value instead.
- Changed source-backed installation from copied trees to symlinks. Skills and authored Claude
  agents stay live from the authoritative repository clone; only native agent projections without
  an authored target-format source are generated as regular files.
- Removed installer profiles, receipts, version comparison, ownership hashes, pruning, status
  reports, and hidden atomic backup paths. Installation writes only selected platform skill and
  agent entries; matching entries stay untouched and mismatches are replaced from Git.
- The final six-pass audit removed unused target source-contract metadata and the unused
  implicit-primary planning path, and made the root executable the documented install command.
  The explicit Codex target now uses skills and links each canonical category once,
  matching the local skills installer contract and grouped skill discovery. Claude
  remains flat under skills; Cursor uses skills, and OpenCode uses its native
  global skills root. The shared skills compatibility root is unused.
- Repaired package.json identity while preserving the upstream TypeScript front doors and their
  canonical aliases.

### Decisions and Failures

- A six-pass pre-merge audit found that existing propagation-owned test_*.py files were
  changed locally for the discovery migration. Those edits remain a durability risk until the
  upstream template is changed and propagated or a compatible local boundary is retained.
- Recorded KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) as a top-level project priority in
  HUMAN_GUIDANCE.md. The audit's hypothetical duplicate-name concern does not
  justify more machinery while the current catalog has no duplicates; revisit it only if an actual
  collision appears.
- Treat the Git repository as current and installed platform directories as stale. The discarded
  receipt design added hidden state for a versioning and ownership problem this installer does not
  need to solve.

### Developer Tests and Notes

- Rotated completed 2026-06-16 through 2026-08-17 day blocks into
  CHANGELOG-2026-08a.md after the active changelog crossed the
  repository's 1,000-line limit.
- Refreshed README.md, CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md, and
  FILE_STRUCTURE.md to document the canonical category, sidecar, agent,
  target, generator, and installer model. Installation and usage verification now include the
  universal OpenAI-sidecar contract check.
- Ran the standalone arch-docs workflow after the symlink-installer change. The architecture
  and file-structure docs now distinguish canonical sources, tracked generated artifacts, ignored
  local material, state-free installer output, generated native agents, Codex category links, and
  permanent versus E2E tests.
- Centralized platform agent installation around canonical agents/ Markdown and
  CATALOG.yaml. AGENTS_INDEX.md supplies searchable
  role metadata, while target-specific agent files are rendered only during installation.
- Regenerated the skills index, platform manifests, and searchable agent index from canonical
  repository data. USAGE.md records the generator checks, focused validation command,
  and primary adapter E2E command.
- Audited the platform test plan against the permanent-test checklist. Removed the redundant
  interview parser tests, duplicate-target diagnostic-priority case, tunable sidecar-length
  assertion, compatibility lifecycle repetition, and unused one-test E2E bulk runner; restored
  pre-existing tests where category work had introduced collection-count or tautological checks.
  A second strict pass removed thin wrapper, tunable category-order, overlapping diagnostic, and
  private state-parser cases, plus broad/redundant hygiene exemptions. The independent test
  audit then removed a redundant operating-system symlink test and an E2E wording assertion.
- Completed release-gate verification after the guided symlink-installer correction:  passed 3,708 tests; the permanent primary E2E passed in an isolated temporary home; all
  generated-output and OpenAI-sidecar checks passed; whitespace checks passed. The completion
  record is in
  platform_skills_completion_report.md.

entries:
### Additions and New Features

- Added a universal .graphifyignore seed that excludes , , , and
   from Graphify repository maps. It propagates to every repo only when absent,
  preserving repository-specific additions after bootstrap.

### Fixes and Maintenance

- Added  to gitignore.universal, the canonical source for the
  propagation-managed UNIVERSAL .gitignore block. This preserves Graphify output ignores
  across future propagation runs.
- Added the pytestqt to pytest-qt import-distribution alias to
  test_import_requirements.py.
- Added canonical import-distribution aliases for applefoundationmodels, bricklink,
  exiftool, graphify, markdown_it, material, screencapturekit, and skimage.
- Added the canonical graphifyy[ollama,sql,terraform] PyPI development requirement. This installs
  Graphify's complete base dependency set plus the Ollama backend used by
  graphify_map_repo.sh, the tree-sitter-sql parser needed for authored database schemas,
  and the tree-sitter-hcl parser needed for Terraform repositories, without unrelated optional
  integrations. This keeps the dependency inventory explicit under ASVS 15.1.2 and 15.2.4.
- Corrected the stale propagation test that still classified root  as template metadata.
  Root tools are universal consumer tools under the current location-based routing policy.

### Developer Tests and Notes

- Confirmed from the graphifyy 0.9.48 wheel metadata that the package requires Python 3.10+,
  its ollama extra adds the openai client, its sql extra adds tree-sitter-sql, and its
  terraform extra adds tree-sitter-hcl.
- Confirmed the native Graphify ignore matcher excludes all four universal paths and the
  propagation plan routes .graphifyignore to noexist_files for every declared repo type.
- The complete pytest suite passes with 1723 tests. Direct ASCII checks and git diff --check
  also pass for the changed files.

entries:
### Decisions and failures - Corrected the root attached-cyclohexane E2E's offscreen menu boundary without changing product behavior. It opens the real Edit menu, proves the unique, visible, enabled shared attach QAction, and activates its popup row through QTest press/release rather than direct QAction.trigger() or unsupported popup-menu Return dispatch on offscreen QPA. - Guarded attached-cyclohexane release with its retained durable anchor. A malformed pending C6 intent without start_atom_id now retires the native receipt through the normal cancellation lifecycle, presents one refusal, and cannot commit or mutate the document; the existing generic start-scene rule remains unchanged. - Fixed a release-handler guard that made a valid Attach Cyclohexane Ring drag return before native commit because this gesture intentionally has no generic start_scene. The exception is limited to C6 attachment; existing regular ring releases with a missing start scene still refuse without mutation. The focused Qt coverage now proves one native commit and one revision transition. - Repaired the root attached-cyclohexane E2E's generated child program: the bridge-call wrapper now has valid nested indentation, and the outer test compiles its exact dedented child source before execution so a child-only syntax error cannot be misreported as a successful parent run. - Extended the existing attached-cyclohexane root E2E's post-release failure payload without changing its gesture or one-transition assertion. A failure now distinguishes the installed Qt snapshot from the authoritative native-session snapshot, records the real commit-and-refresh outcome or its typed exception, and includes active intent plus typed refusal-recorder facts. - Added bounded, test-local attached-cyclohexane E2E diagnostics for a cleared drag. Its existing real menu-to-viewport interaction now reports passive focus snapshots, presence-only intent state, begin/preview call counts and caught exception summaries, plus typed refusal facts when no native receipt appears. It changes neither product code nor the drag behavior. - Corrected the root attached-cyclohexane E2E's real menu-route activation. It now waits for the selected popup to become visible and its target action to be selectable, then proves the checkable action armed after the popup click. Bounded failures record only menu and action state; no direct action trigger or product fallback was added. - Restored the expected bare build.sh developer command. Native builds now use the builder-owned, profile-scoped managed source-archive cache below : missing hash-pinned HTTPS archives are atomically provisioned once, verified cache reuse is offline, and explicit sealed/archive overrides remain strict. The default never selects a previous output or a nonexistent checkout cache. - Kept the root attached-cyclohexane E2E fully unattended without changing Ferrum's interactive modal policy. Its generated offscreen window now records only that instance's typed edit refusal for the intentional ineligible-anchor click, then proves exactly one refusal with unchanged document and settled action state. - Added failure-only, redacted diagnostics to the existing ineligible-anchor attached-cyclohexane E2E assertion. A refusal mismatch now reports typed request presence facts, before/after snapshot identity facts, and C6 action/intent state without serializing CDML or the input path. - Closed the attached-cyclohexane implicit-anchor picker test gap without new infrastructure. The focused Qt test now proves a rendered hit takes precedence over the C6-only nearby-projection fallback, and an ambiguous visible Attach Cyclohexane Ring press leaves both the durable start atom and opaque native receipt unset. - Fixed Attach Cyclohexane Ring targeting for ordinary unlabelled carbon atoms. The action preserves normal rendered-atom hit behavior, then only for that action accepts one unique nearest current projection atom within six viewport pixels; equal, absent, and out-of-range candidates refuse without guessing. Generic picking behavior is unchanged. - Corrected the focused attached-cyclohexane Qt test teardown. After its successful C6 commit, the test now uses the public tab undo path and proves the saved CDML and clean state before closing, avoiding the intended interactive dirty-close dialog in an offscreen run. - Added value-safe failure diagnostics to the existing root attached-cyclohexane E2E preview assertion. On a missing native receipt it now reports only action/tool activation and presence-level gesture lifecycle facts; it neither changes product behavior nor adds a harness. - Corrected the attached-cyclohexane E2E wheel-member preflight regex so it selects the direct native .so member before retaining the existing venv path, native-suffix, and SHA-256 provenance checks. - Strengthened the existing single root attached-cyclohexane E2E without adding a harness or fixture. Its Escape branch now first proves a live opaque native receipt and copied preview, while its ineligible-anchor branch proves attach mode was armed and reaches a terminal unarmed refusal with no document mutation. - Removed the unused public attached-cyclohexane candidate revision/digest accessor. The typed internal receipt now exposes only its copied paint preview; prepared document state remains opaque until the document session commits or retires the transaction. - Corrected attached-cyclohexane pointer-move dispatch. The Qt controller now begins the Rust-owned preparation before its generic preview/start-scene guard, which intentionally does not apply to this gesture. The focused offscreen behavior test requires the resulting opaque receipt and paint-only preview after a real pointer move. - Strengthened WP-C1's focused offline Qt lifecycle proof. The existing regular-ring module now records the real cancellation bridge receipt on tab switch, stale-document, and _close_tab_at disposal routes; it also proves one retained receipt survives a refused cancellation and retires exactly once on a direct disposal retry without document mutation. The bridge confinement oracle now scans every Python file beneath the Qt application package, allowing only the controller and this test module. - Repaired WP-C1 attached-cyclohexane cancellation ownership. A Rust cancellation refusal now retains the opaque receipt in a terminal blocked gesture, retires only the disposable Qt overlay, fences all later mutation, and permits retry through the existing cancellation route. Tab-close and application-close paths now refuse disposal while that receipt remains live. The focused offline Qt module covers cancellation refusal/retry plus tab, stale-document, and close retirement routes; its bridge oracle now requires exactly one use of each permitted cooperative bridge method. - Aligned WP-B1's attached-cyclohexane bridge with its concrete cross-crate contract. The pending C6 transaction is now re-exported as a documented internal Rust seam for ferrum-api, while its implementation module remains rustdoc-hidden and fields remain opaque. The real registered Python module test now proves the pending type and any module-level attachment constructor or service remain absent. - Corrected WP-B1's Rust authority claim. The extension still does not register PyPendingAttachedCyclohexaneV1, and its receipt remains Python-opaque, nonconstructible, and serialization-free. The C6 lifecycle is instead an honest public typed internal document seam required by the current crate dependency direction; opaque fields and document session/fence invariants, rather than impossible cross-crate Rust privacy, protect its transaction semantics. A generic prepared-edit framework and session-host migration remain deferred pending evidence. - Corrected WP-C1's planned literal cooperative-bridge call-site oracle: it scans only Qt production and Qt test source trees, excluding Rust binding definitions and tests. This makes it a Qt repository-usage check rather than an impossible restriction on the Rust definitions it intentionally exercises. - Repaired the planned cyclohexane PyO3 opacity proof before implementation: WP-B1 requires omission of the module registration for PyPendingAttachedCyclohexaneV1, actual Python receipt opacity, the documented typed Rust transaction seam with opaque state, and a literal offline Qt source/call-site oracle for exactly the four cooperative bridge methods. This remains repository-surface discipline, not a claim of isolation from arbitrary same-process Python. - Corrected WP-B1's PyO3 authority model for the deferred-ID attached-cyclohexane capability. Its four underscore-prefixed calls are a narrow cooperative internal bridge for Ferrum's trusted same-process Qt controller, not access control against arbitrary Python holding a document session. Rust retains the opaque nonconstructible pending value, C6 candidate/topology, target admission, session/revision/digest/anchor/one-use fencing, atomic commit, and retirement; the bridge returns only copied finite vertices and identity-free outcome facts. It adds no general attachment API, serialized receipt, CDML, identifier, CLI, or Qt surface. Compiled shims and process isolation are explicitly deferred as unjustified for this one gesture. - Added WP-A2's concrete deferred-ID attached-cyclohexane document capability. It keeps the accepted C6 geometry private, reserves five atom and six bond IDs only in copied sequences, fences prepare and commit by revision/digest/session origin, and applies the complete same- molecule extension in one history transition. No generic attachment or template API was added. - Corrected the cyclohexane attachment work-package boundary after the atomic-extension review. WP-A1 is now only the private pure C6 geometry and closed anchor-admission probe; WP-A2 owns the concrete PendingAttachedCyclohexaneV1 capability, copied deferred atom/bond ID sequences, revision/digest/session fencing, atomic history commit, stale/cancel/foreign/replay behavior, and real-document nonmutation proof. The selected discipline reserves five atom IDs and six bond IDs only in copied sequences and installs them with the one committed candidate; sequential commits, live preallocation, and generic attachment frameworks remain rejected. - Added WP-A1's private attached-cyclohexane document-core hypothesis. It uses the settled shared-anchor C6 topology, admits only closed neutral-carbon anchor facts before any identity or session mutation, and has two inline deterministic pose/admission probes. No public receipt, API, Qt, CLI, fixture, or attachment framework was introduced. - Reframed cyclohexane attachment WP-A1 after its source-level negative result: the plan now implements the smallest private document-core pose, admission, and candidate hypothesis before exercising its inline probe matrix. This avoids an unowned test geometry duplicate while retaining fixed shared-anchor topology, autonomous proof, and no fixture or framework expansion. - Corrected the cyclohexane attachment plan's autonomous native-wheel prerequisite to use the builder's implemented build subcommand with explicit output and sealed-input roots. The JSON wheel result remains the exact-artifact selection mechanism. - Clarified HUMAN_GUIDANCE.md as concise direct preferences only; repository style and test policy remain in their canonical documents. - Resolved the cyclohexane atom-attachment plan before implementation: Ferrum V1 is strict shared-anchor C6 annulation with five new carbon atoms, six new n1 bonds, and pre-allocation neutral-carbon capacity refusal. The plan now retains the existing detached-ring action and adds a separately named, keyboard-accessible attach action. Its one root E2E is an autonomous fresh native-wheel plus local offscreen-Qt harness with captured diagnostics; no human or network gate remains. ### Changed - Closed the Direct Haworth PyO3 preparation-error mapping: structural SMILES syntax refusals now surface as the existing actionable DirectHaworthInputError, preserving the complete typed domain error match without expanding the unsupported Haworth CLI feature. - Extended the registered C6 PyO3 bridge test to prove that foreign-commit and replay refusals preserve the complete public session snapshot: CDML, revision, digest, and dirty state. - Mapped the generic empty molecule-batch session refusal through the existing closed PyO3 document and direct-Haworth error categories without exposing a new Python detail surface. - Completed and accepted M2a.3a's fixed-target CML/CML2 new_document import. The Rust API keeps CML decoding, conversion, and CDML handoff private, measures exact bounded protocol envelopes before commit, and lets the CLI publish its explicit artifact only after a committed result. Evidence: ferrum-m2a3a-cml-final-evidence.md; independent acceptance: ferrum-m2a3a-final-acceptance-review.md. Append-current, durable selectors, live PyO3/Qt import, export/conversion, and broader CML semantics remain deferred; this does not claim full CML, OASA, or BKChem parity. - Extended the existing generic molecule-batch session-fence test: a batch refused by a foreign session now commits on its owning session as one revision transition containing both prepared records. - Bound M2a.3a's generic prepared molecule batch to its exact process-local document session before token or generated-ID mutation. The existing offline CML CLI E2E now also proves a textual rejected source stays out of both response channels. - Corrected M2a.3a batch preparation so discarded CML candidates leave both generated-ID allocation and provisional-token state unchanged. Moved the public import summary DTO into the protocol contract and made the CML operation module and closed CML response types crate-private. - M2a.3a now keeps CML-specific decode, conversion, and CDML handoff private to the API operation. ferrum-document exposes only an atomic generic molecule batch candidate, and the named CML protocol operation measures its final success and refusal envelopes before committing. - Tightened M2a.3a response admission: the CLI now measures its closed CML refusal envelope through the same bounded path as success, while the existing offline root E2E rejects any refusal stderr or document artifact leakage. ### Additions and New Features - Added the narrow M2a.3a CML open CLI workflow. ferrum open INPUT --format cml --output NEW.cdml [--json] admits one CML source into a new Rust-owned document, measures its bounded canonical summary before exposing CDML, and publishes only the explicit output file. The one offline root E2E writes inline CML to a temporary directory and exercises the real CLI. - Corrected M2a.2 CML document admission proof and refusal mapping. A compact inline two-record CML test now reaches the document prepare seam and proves a late document-owned identity failure preserves the revision, digest, history, projection, and generated-ID state. Candidate serialization failures now map to the distinct redacted serialization_failed refusal rather than internal_failure. - Added M2a.2's in-memory CML document-admission seam. It transforms decoded source coordinates into Ferrum document coordinates before identity allocation, commits every admitted record as one atomic transaction, and maps decoder and document failures to a redacted internal refusal seam. Inline Rust tests prove transformed batch admission and a late refusal leaves the document, history, and projection unchanged. ### Decisions and Failures - Kept M2a.3a deliberately small. Decoder and document-admission failures now retain their exact closed refusal reason through CML open rather than being coarsened to invalid_xml; no CML fixtures, corpus, network path, generic conversion route, selector, live receipt, or Qt action was added. - Re-scoped the next M2a.3a delivery to one stateless new_document CML open operation and one ferrum open INPUT --format cml --output NEW.cdml [--json] workflow. Append-current-document, durable selectors, live PyO3 receipts, Qt actions, corpus/fixtures, and generic import machinery remain separate later slices. The canonical envelope is still admitted before document/output publication under the existing 1 MiB bound, and the sole CLI E2E stays offline in root . - Recorded the KISS decision rule in HUMAN_GUIDANCE.md: prefer the smallest durable architecture and proof set, and require a concrete current use before adding machinery. - Added M2a.1's Rust-owned closed CML1/CML2 tokenizer and bounded source-graph decoder. It admits only the documented simple-molecule profiles, returns redacted typed refusals before document mutation, preserves source-space coordinates for document-owned conversion, and uses compact inline Rust coverage without CML fixtures or external execution.
- Corrected M2a.1 CML/CML2 closed-profile admission: CML2 atom and bond children now refuse at the frame boundary, and XML entity decoding consumes each caller-supplied UTF-8 output budget before allocation or append. - Corrected M2a.0 CML/CML2 repository conformance. Removed the premature committed fixture corpus, manifests, hash-inventory harness, and its chemistry-only test dependencies. M2a.0 now retains compact in-process registry, typed-refusal, DTO, and budget relationship coverage only. - Added M2a.0's Rust-owned CML/CML2 import foundation: a cross-layer registry, closed request/refusal/budget DTOs, and a private response-budget value reserved for M2a.3's future exact-envelope admission. This phase adds no XML parser, document mutation, canonical response admission, CLI route, PyO3 receipt, or Qt action. - Corrected the M2a CML/CML2 import contract's response channel. The 8 MiB Rust-private candidate is no longer contradictory with the 1 MiB public JSON envelope: import is explicitly control-plane only, and success returns only bounded summary, provenance, revision/digest, loss facts, and durable molecule selectors. Complete CDML, candidate CDML, source CML, and converted artifacts cannot cross either protocol or CLI result channel. Explicit CLI --output remains atomic post-success document publication; non-JSON output is bounded status/summary only. Any artifact-delivery route requires a separately named conversion/export contract. - Replaced the provisional M2a CML/CML2 design with a closed import-only contract. It now freezes namespace/root/container grammar, XML lexical behavior, CML array-attribute refusal, a y-down CML to y-up Ferrum coordinate transform, every budget/refusal triple, public-selector versus live-receipt ownership, a real cross-layer format registry, fixtures, and proof gates. - Accepted the M4b Rust SMARTS parity milestone after independent backend, named-CLI, private-live-bridge, and isolated packaged Qt dock evidence. The final GUI receipt covers raw and direct-root selected queries, ownership handoff, result replay/retirement, mutation/reprojection, Save As/reopen, and tab switching. M4b completion does not claim broader OASA/BKChem parity or release readiness; M2a CML/CML2 interchange is the next recommended work. - Made FerrumNativeMainWindow the sole owner of outgoing SMARTS tab retirement. A real tab switch now clears and hides copied dock state only after one native retirement attempt, unbinds the outgoing callback, and binds the incoming tab without touching its published plan. Failure clears stale UI without retrying native retirement; first-tab activation and document mutation remain non-hiding. - Corrected first native-tab activation to re-enter the authoritative tab lifecycle only after registration publishes the page mapping. Added a bounded queued Open helper and two-tab SMARTS regression proving outgoing receipt retirement and incoming direct queryability. - Corrected Qt native-tab activation to retire only the outgoing live SMARTS render plan. A newly admitted tab now retains its already-installed plan, while the outgoing tab's opaque receipt remains invalidated. Added an asynchronous two-tab regression that proves the incoming tab queries immediately without a repair observation. - Corrected the Qt native-tab test session so receipt-only SMARTS cleanup no longer models full render-plan retirement. The fixture regression now proves receipt clearing permits a same-plan rerun, while full retirement refuses it. - Made current stale SMARTS delivery retirement fail closed. A failed native receipt-only retirement now raises the typed refresh-required error instead of reporting that the delivery was dropped, while retaining the opaque receipt and unavailable state for safe recovery. The direct-session audit explicitly classifies both private SMARTS retirement entry points. - Split private live SMARTS retirement into receipt-only query cleanup and full render-plan lifecycle retirement. Clear, rerun, stale delivery, and second Escape now revoke every opaque receipt without unpublishing an unchanged drawing's authoritative plan; mutation, reprojection, deactivation, and disposal still revoke both plan and receipts. - Corrected SMARTS selected-molecule canvas capture to use Rust's direct-root interaction observation and point-selection boundary. A molecule glyph click now produces the compatible opaque selected-query token without Python atom to molecule inference; focused Qt coverage rejects the structural-child path. - Made Qt pointer-tool action handoff invoke SMARTS selected-root cancellation and the real command handler through one ordered dispatch slot; added a real Add Atom integration regression. - Corrected the SMARTS Query action's selected-molecule capture focus policy. Opening the modeless dock now leaves an armed canvas choice focused and active, while a later registered canvas-tool handoff still retires it before its handler takes ownership. - Corrected SMARTS dock ownership: each Ferrum window now retains the single base-created dock/controller/action, while only the capture owner holds a selected-query token. The dock carries copied readiness through deferred UI work and consumes the token synchronously only at query admission. - Replaced SMARTS selected-molecule capture's one-time QAction scan with an explicit main-window interaction-action handoff. Current and future pointer-owning tool actions now retire capture before their own handler runs. - Corrected modeless SMARTS dock closed-error decoding. It now accepts only exact frozen PyO3 category/reason/recovery enum triples, maps every native closed outcome to user-facing recovery guidance, and fails unknown or incomplete outcomes closed as typed unavailability. - Corrected SMARTS dock lifecycle refresh, document-transition invalidation, and Escape coverage so stale copied results clear immediately after a successful mutation or render-plan replacement without issuing another native retirement.

repositories.description: A pre-alpha CDML chemical drawing platform for scientists and educators that combines a retained PySide6 desktop editor with a planned Rust chemistry backend for durable document ownership.

readme.summary:
Ferrum is a Rust chemical-document tool for inspecting, validating, rewriting, rendering,
converting, and drawing durable CDML records.

repositories.description: a Python tool that tracks a runner in track meet video and produces a cropped, stabilized "virtual dolly camera" output. Users place seed annotations on key frames, and the solver propagates tracking between seeds to produce a smooth cropped video that follows the athlete.

readme.summary: A Python tool for track-meet videographers that produces a cropped, stabilized virtual-dolly output following a single athlete. Users place a handful of seed annotations; the solver propagates geometry between seeds across the full race.
